label: UniFi U7 Pro
description: Tri-band Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) ceiling AP with 2x2 MU-MIMO on 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz (6 spatial streams, up to 5.8 Gbps in 6 GHz). It has one 1/2.5GbE RJ45 port with 802.3at PoE+ and three radios: 2.4, 5 and 6 GHz.
notes:
PoE+ (802.3at), 21W max consumption. Single 2.5GbE port; 320 MHz channels and the 5.8 Gbps 6 GHz rate are far beyond a 2.5G uplink, so it is backhaul-limited.

The 25.5 W this port used to carry is not Ubiquiti's figure: it is the 802.3at PD class ceiling, written as if the box drew all of it, and the note above has said "21W max consumption" all along. Read 2026-11-28 from https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/wifi/u7-pro (HTTP 200, 658,469 B), the same page: "Power Method: PoE+" and "Max. Power Consumption: 21W". poeIn is now that 21 W, and the Power Method row also settles two capabilities the spec omitted - PoE+ is 802.3at, and a box powered from its uplink is a poe-pd. Nothing in the engine compares a PD draw with the class its PSE declared, so a 21 W AP on an 802.3af port is still accepted; what the figure changes is the budget arithmetic the PoE lab reports.
